CMS National Correct Coding Initiative Policy Manual
Chapter 1, Section 3: Modifier 25 and Same-Day Minor Procedures (placeholder)

This is a placeholder reference document for the v1 demo. Real corpus
ingestion (T109) substitutes this file with the official CMS NCCI Policy
Manual chapters covering E/M services and Modifier 25.

Modifier 25 is appended to an Evaluation and Management service to indicate
that on the day a procedure or service identified by another HCPCS or CPT
code was performed, the patient's condition required a significant,
separately identifiable Evaluation and Management service above and beyond
the usual preoperative and postoperative care associated with that
procedure or service. The E/M service must be supported by documentation
that meets the relevant level of service. The decision to perform a minor
procedure during the same encounter does not by itself qualify the visit
for a separate E/M service.

A separately identifiable E/M service must be supported by a distinct
problem. When the chief complaint is solely the indication for the
procedure, Modifier 25 is not appropriate. When the chief complaint
identifies an unrelated or new problem that requires evaluation, the
E/M service may be reported with Modifier 25 if the documentation
supports the level of service billed.

When the E/M and the procedure are performed on different anatomic sites,
both LT/RT or T1 through T9 modifiers should be appended to the
procedure code in addition to Modifier 25

supports the level of service billed.

both LT/RT or T1 through T9 modifiers should be appended to the
procedure code in addition to Modifier 25 on the E/M service. Site-
specific documentation in the encounter note is required.

CMS MLN Matters Bulletin: Modifier 25 with Minor Procedures (placeholder)

This is a placeholder reference document. Real corpus ingestion (T109)
substitutes the actual MLN Matters article.

Background. Payers continue to scrutinize claims that pair an Evaluation
and Management service with a minor procedure on the same date. Modifier
25 is the standard mechanism to indicate a significant, separately
identifiable E/M service. Practices billing Modifier 25 on more than 50
percent of procedural claims have historically been subject to Pre-
Payment Reviews.

Documentation requirements. The E/M note must demonstrate a distinct
chief complaint, separate exam findings, and an independent medical
decision. A note that reads as procedure-only workup will not support
the modifier under audit.

Common pitfalls. Submitting Modifier 25 when the chief complaint is the
procedure indication. Documenting an exam limited to the procedure site.
Documenting medical decision making that addresses only the procedure.
Each of these failure modes is independently sufficient to disallow the
E/M service.

AAPC Modifier 25 Educational Series (placeholder)

This is a placeholder. Real corpus ingestion replaces this file with the
publicly accessible AAPC educational article (paywalled content is not
ingested).

Modifier 25 indicates that on the day a procedure or service was
performed, the patient's condition required a significant, separately
identifiable Evaluation and Management service above and beyond the
usual preoperative and postoperative care.

Tips for documentation:

- The chief complaint must name a problem that is distinct from the
  procedure's primary indication. A chief complaint that reads as the
  procedure indication does not establish separability.
- Exam findings must include observations on at least one body part or
  condition that is not the procedure site. Generic statements of
  unremarkable findings are not sufficient.
- The medical decision making must reflect an independent judgment with
  risks, data review, and a management plan distinct from the procedure
  decision.
- When the E/M and procedure are at different anatomic sites, append the
  appropriate LT/RT or T1 to T9 modifier in addition to Modifier 25.

AAPC FAQ: E/M with Minor Procedures (placeholder)

This is a placeholder. Real corpus ingestion replaces with the publicly
accessible AAPC FAQ article.

Q: Does the decision to perform the procedure itself qualify as a
separately identifiable E/M service?

A: No. The decision-to-perform component of a minor procedure is bundled
into the procedure's pre-operative work. To support Modifier 25, the
documentation must establish that the E/M service addressed a problem
distinct from that decision.

Q: Can the same provider bill an E/M and a minor procedure on the same
day for the same patient?

A: Yes, when the documentation supports a distinct problem and the
related history, exam, and medical decision making meet the level of
service billed. Modifier 25 must be appended to the E/M service.

Q: What about same-site E/M and procedure?

A: When both services occur at the same anatomic site, the documentation
must establish a separable problem that is independent of the procedure.
Without that, the E/M service is not separately reportable.

JARALL Knowledge Center: Modifier 25 Mastery (placeholder)

This is a placeholder. Real corpus ingestion replaces with the actual
April 23, 2026 JARALL Modifier 25 Mastery article.

The JARALL Standard for Modifier 25 defensibility rests on four criteria:

1. Distinct Chief Complaint. The chief complaint must name a problem
   distinct from the procedure's primary indication. A chief complaint
   that reads as the procedure indication is a categorical failure.

2. Separate Exam Findings. The exam must document findings on a body
   part or condition not addressed by the procedure. Generic statements
   are insufficient.

3. Independent Medical Decision Making. The medical decision making
   must address a problem with risks, data, and management options
   independent of the procedure decision.

4. Site-Specificity. When the E/M and procedure are at different
   anatomic sites, both LT/RT or T1 to T9 modifiers must appear on the
   claim and the documentation must support the site distinction.

Each of these criteria stands on its own. A note that fails any one of
them does not support Modifier 25 under audit. Practices using Modifier
25 on more than 50 percent of procedural claims face Pre-Payment Reviews
in 2026 and beyond.

JARALL Knowledge Center: 2026 E/M Shift (placeholder)

This is a placeholder. Real corpus ingestion replaces with the actual
March 25, 2026 JARALL E/M shift article.

The 2026 E/M reimbursement shift increases scrutiny on documentation
that supports a separately identifiable E/M service. The Centers for
Medicare and Medicaid Services along with major commercial payers
continue to deploy AI-driven claim review for Modifier 25 utilization.

Practical implications for podiatry practices:

- Documentation defensibility is now a revenue cycle issue. A note that
  cannot defend an attached Modifier 25 will lose the E/M reimbursement
  on appeal, costing time and money.
- Provider-level utilization analytics are increasingly common. A
  practice with greater than 50 percent of procedural claims attaching
  Modifier 25 should expect Pre-Payment Reviews.
- Coder review before claim submission is the most cost-effective
  defense. A second-opinion check that scores defensibility against the
  four-criterion JARALL Standard catches weak documentation early.
